adr: ADR-160 D7 — a medium is a named record, and a force model declares what it needs
what: OCEAN-LAB'S COPY of the committed medium rows. ADR-160 D3 forbids a runtime import between packages, so this lab carries the rows as data and implements the media it can answer for. A lab may differ only in what it can ANSWER (the implementation block), never in what a medium's properties ARE: the `properties` of every row here must equal embodied's committed row (embodied/src-routes/engine/medium/medium-properties.json), and scripts/check-adr160-contract.mjs fails when they, the row keys or the implementation keys drift.
notWhat: Not a second answer to what seawater is. The property values are embodied's row, pinned by the contract check; the only thing this file adds is ocean-lab's implementation of seawater: a free surface at the datum and the sea-state heave field the wave-propulsion model takes.

units.gravityMps2: m/s^2, a vector in the plant's world frame (x, y, z), z up
units.dynamicViscosityPaS: Pa*s — dynamic, because that is what an atmosphere model produces (mu_Pas). Kinematic viscosity is mu/rho and is DERIVED, never stored here (D7)
units.speedOfSoundMs: m/s, null when the medium cannot answer — never defaulted
units.temperatureK: K, null when the medium cannot answer — never defaulted
units.heightM: metres above the medium's own datum, positive up. The validity coordinate.

earthSurfaceGravitySource: embodied's committed row (earthSurfaceGravityMps2), carried verbatim and pinned by the contract check.

vacuum.label: Vacuum (Earth surface gravity)
vacuum.summary: No fluid at all. Nothing in this lab produces a force in it, and the wave-propulsion model declines it by its envelope.

validity.why: The same band embodied's row declares: gravity is the only property this medium has, and it holds to 3.1e-4 relative over +/-1000 m of the datum.

provenance.dynamicViscosityPaS: Zero by definition — embodied's row. Kinematic viscosity mu/rho is 0/0 and is UNAVAILABLE, never zero.

air.label: Air (ISA sea level)
air.summary: Standard-atmosphere air at the sea-level station, as embodied's row carries it. It has no free surface, so nothing in this lab can heave against it.

field.why: This lab models no wind. A still field is an answer by name, not a silent zero.

validity.why: The band embodied's row chose for a constant sea-level station: within about 1 % over the surface layer, refused outside rather than extrapolated. aero-lab's atmosphere resolves the column.

provenance.dynamicViscosityPaS: embodied's row (Sutherland at 288.15 K from aero-lab's constants).
provenance.speedOfSoundMs: embodied's row (sqrt(gamma R T0) from aero-lab's constants).

seawater.label: Seawater (coastal, free surface)
seawater.summary: Constant-density coastal seawater with a free surface at the datum and a sea-state heave field. This is the medium the explorer's wave-propulsion model runs in; embodied's row carries the same properties and neither of these two fields.

field.why: The surface heaves at w(t) = (H/2)(2*pi/T)cos(2*pi*t/T) for the sea state a site names (the report's WAVE INPUT). The heights, periods and occurrences are the SITE's, carried on the design vector, not this row's; no current field is modelled here.

freeSurface.why: The float follows a free surface at the datum; the sub runs submerged below it on its tether. This plane is what the wave-propulsion model asks for, and it is what air and vacuum do not have.

validity.why: From the free surface down: the float sits at the datum and the sub at the tether's depth. Above the surface this row has no answer; 1000 m is the same floor embodied's row chose for a constant-density column with no pressure law.

provenance.densityKgM3: embodied's row, which is ocean-lab's own SEAWATER_DENSITY_KGM3 (marine/services/power-budget.ts and rotor-design/services/rotor-presets.ts, pinned by scripts/check-medium-properties.mjs). The explorer study's 24.1 L giving 24.7 kg of buoyancy is 0.0241 m^3 * 1025 kg/m^3.
provenance.dynamicViscosityPaS: embodied's row: 1025 kg/m^3 * 1.05e-6 m^2/s (ocean-lab SEAWATER_KINEMATIC_VISCOSITY_M2S, rotor-design/services/section-polar.ts).
